report.answer_text:
Sanae Takaichi’s 2025 economic agenda paired short-term relief from rising prices with longer-term public investment to raise wages and growth. She called this “responsible and proactive” fiscal policy: spend now on targeted measures, while aiming to lower Japan’s debt-to-GDP ratio by growing the economy faster than public debt. (japan.kantei.go.jp)
Cost-of-living relief. Her government proposed ending the temporary gasoline and diesel tax surcharges, subsidizing winter electricity and gas bills, paying ¥20,000 per child, and giving local governments more money to help households with rising food prices. (bf.emb-japan.go.jp)
Income-tax relief. In December, her government proposed raising the annual income-tax threshold from ¥1.6 million to ¥1.78 million and linking key deductions to inflation. It also began designing a refundable tax credit for low- and middle-income households. (investing.com)
Higher wages and business investment. She proposed helping small businesses invest in labor-saving equipment and pass higher costs on to customers so they could afford wage increases. She also backed public-private investment in AI, semiconductors, shipbuilding, and quantum technology, along with stronger supply chains for critical materials. (japan.kantei.go.jp)
The centerpiece was the November 21, 2025 stimulus package: ¥21.3 trillion in new fiscal measures, including tax cuts, or ¥25.5 trillion once government investment and loan programs were included. (japan.kantei.go.jp)

quotes.text: We will swiftly and without fail bring a sense of security to people in their daily lives.

While it is essential to have wage increases that surpass the rise in prices, leaving the matter entirely up to businesses only results in making it difficult for business operators to run their companies.
we will compile measures rapidly and submit the necessary supplementary budget to the Diet.
Strategic investments that enhance resilience against potential crises are the core focus of the Takaichi Cabinet's growth strategy.
